instruction:
Two-software CAE flow: SolidWorks -> Abaqus/CAE. For this task, use the SOLIDWORKS 2025 and Abaqus CAE shortcuts on the desktop for the two stages of this workflow. No init file is provided; start from a new blank SolidWorks part.

Chain evidence requirement: use the design token EW_SW_ABQ_02. Keep this token encoded in the SolidWorks part/custom properties or STEP export metadata so the text of stage1_geometry.step contains EW_SW_ABQ_02 and SOLIDWORKS_TO_ABAQUS. In Abaqus/CAE, create at least one model, part, instance, set, surface, job description, or other native name containing both EW_SW_ABQ_02 and IMPORTED_FROM_stage1_geometry.step, so the final CAE file carries evidence that Abaqus consumed the SolidWorks STEP handoff.

1. In SolidWorks, use sketch and feature tools to create a center-hole tensile coupon. Geometry requirements: overall length 120 mm, width 30 mm, thickness 3 mm, a D12 through hole at the geometric center, and straight grip regions at both ends. Export the completed CAD geometry to C:\Users\user\Desktop\stage1_geometry.step.
2. In Abaqus/CAE, import stage1_geometry.step and create the finite-element model. Use the model name Model-HoleTension. Define material Steel with E=210000 MPa and nu=0.3, create a solid section using Steel, and assign it to the coupon. Create a Static General analysis step named Step-Tension. Create sets named LEFT_GRIP, RIGHT_GRIP, and HOLE_EDGE. Use a coarse global seed with modest local seeding only around HOLE_EDGE, and use first-order linear solid elements such as C3D8R where practical or coarse C3D4 where needed; do not use quadratic elements. Create a boundary condition named BC-LeftGrip that fixes LEFT_GRIP. Create an action named Load-RightTension: either an approximately +1 kN axial tensile load on RIGHT_GRIP, or an equivalent named axial displacement boundary condition on RIGHT_GRIP. Submit the job named Job-HoleTension and wait for the analysis to complete.
3. Required deliverables on the Desktop: C:\Users\user\Desktop\stage1_geometry.step, C:\Users\user\Desktop\Job-HoleTension.cae, and C:\Users\user\Desktop\Job-HoleTension.odb. Do not create extra STEP, DXF, CAE, or ODB deliverables.

 First use SolidWorks to create and export the CAD STEP file, then use Abaqus/CAE to import that STEP file, build the finite-element model, submit the job, and save the CAE and ODB deliverables. Software launch locations: SOLIDWORKS 2025: `C:\Users\Public\Desktop\SOLIDWORKS 2025.lnk`; Abaqus/CAE: `C:\Users\user\Desktop\Abaqus CAE.lnk`.
